author: high
claim: Let \(G\) be a finite undirected graph. Prove that \(G\) is bipartite if and only if \(G\) contains no cycle of odd length.

verification_report.summary: The proof correctly establishes both implications. In the bipartite-to-no-odd-cycle direction, alternating between the two vertex classes forces every cycle to have even length. In the converse direction, the proof constructs a spanning tree in each connected component, partitions vertices by parity of their tree depth, and shows that any edge with same-parity endpoints would combine with the even-length tree path between them to form an odd cycle. The componentwise partitions therefore give a bipartition of the whole graph. The argument is self-contained and contains no critical errors, gaps, prohibited justification patterns, or references requiring validation.
